note:
Every ABSENT finding scripts/check-engine-signatures.mjs currently reports against main, keyed by class+method (not line number: an edit that only shifts lines shouldn't need a baseline update; a NEW call site elsewhere to an already-baselined pair is intentionally absorbed too -- the checker prints this baseline's own coverage every run so that absorption stays visible instead of silent). Reviewed and classified 2026-08-30 by reading each call site in context, not from the finding alone. Two categories, and they mean different things -- see each entry's own `category`:

  harmless-dead-code: the check is RIGHT -- the method genuinely does not exist -- and the code already knows it (a documented multi-build fallback probe, or a guarded branch whose earlier sibling already succeeds). PanelBridge.lua does not need to change for these.

  tool-limitation: the check is WRONG. This checker only resolves a receiver's STATICALLY DECLARED type, never the real runtime concrete type -- so a call through an interface-typed accessor (e.g. SandboxOptions.getOptionByName(), declared to return the SandboxOption interface) is checked against the interface, not whatever concrete subtype is actually handed back at runtime. Do not treat entries in this category as debt to clean up; the call site already works.

Adding a NEW method here should be rare and deliberate -- it means 'I looked at this specific finding and decided the code, not the checker, is correct as-is', not 'suppress this to turn the gate green'. A finding that is a real, previously-unknown bug (e.g. player.setLx/setLy/setLz below -- undocumented before this checker existed) still belongs in the harmless-dead-code category once someone has actually confirmed it's inert, exactly like the rest of this file; it does NOT get fixed here, since scripts/ is not where PanelBridge.lua gets edited.

Dead fallback in a multi-tier vehicle-removal chain (permanentlyRemove -> removeFromWorld -> vehicle:removeVehicle -> cell:removeVehicle -> error). BaseVehicle's own permanentlyRemove()/removeFromWorld(), tried first in the same chain, both genuinely exist (verified via javap) and succeed before this branch is ever reached.

getOptionByName() is statically declared to return the SandboxOption INTERFACE, which has no setValue -- but the real object handed back at runtime is always a concrete subtype (e.g. IntegerSandboxOption), which inherits setValue(int) from an entirely different class, zombie.config.IntegerConfigOption (verified directly via javap on the concrete type). This checker only resolves a receiver's statically declared type, never the runtime concrete type, so it cannot see past the interface here. The call site already works; do not "fix" it.

Optional B41/B42 fallback after the global addSound() path. This B42 build has no IsoWorld.getWorldSoundManager(); PanelBridge.invoke is guarded and the handler returns a clear failure instead of crashing when neither sound API exists.

getOptionByName()/getOptionByIndex() are statically declared to return the SandboxOption INTERFACE, while the runtime objects are concrete Boolean/Integer/Double/Enum/StringSandboxOption subtypes that provide the value accessors. The checker does not resolve runtime subtype dispatch; the existing calls are wrapped by PanelBridge.tryGet and are the handler's primary value path.

The receiver is the SandboxOption interface, but the runtime enum/integer subtype is concrete and may provide this optional accessor. PanelBridge.tryGet treats absence as a normal fallback to getValue, so this is a reviewed interface-resolution limitation, not an unguarded engine call.

getClass() is inherited from java.lang.Object and is available on the Java object at runtime, but the committed engine manifest records the resolved SandboxOption hierarchy rather than Object's universal methods. The call is already guarded by PanelBridge.invoke.

The receiver is statically the SandboxOption interface; enum concrete subtypes provide enum-count metadata. The call is optional, wrapped in pcall/tryGet, and only enriches enum metadata when available.

The receiver is statically the SandboxOption interface, while the runtime enum subtype owns this optional enum-label accessor. PanelBridge.tryGet tolerates its absence and the surrounding pcall makes the metadata enrichment non-fatal.

Numeric concrete sandbox-option subtypes provide bounds, but getOptionByName()/getOptionByIndex() expose only the SandboxOption interface to this static checker. The call is optional and guarded by tryGet.
Numeric concrete sandbox-option subtypes provide bounds, but the static receiver is the SandboxOption interface. The call is optional and guarded by tryGet; missing bounds simply omit metadata.

Concrete sandbox-option subtypes provide default values behind the SandboxOption interface. PanelBridge.tryGet treats the accessor as optional and serializes the value only when a runtime subtype supplies it.

The option name is provided by the concrete ConfigOption-derived runtime object, but the accessor is reached through the SandboxOption interface in this file. The call is wrapped by safeStr/PanelBridge.invoke and is not an unguarded engine dependency.

The checker has no Lua scope tracking and reuses an unrelated whole-file obj type from getSandboxOptions(). At both call sites here, obj is an IsoLightSwitch proven by instanceof before setLightSwitchState() runs; the SandboxOptions receiver classification is false.

The checker has no Lua scope tracking and misclassifies the setLightSwitchState() obj parameter as SandboxOptions. The actual receiver is an IsoLightSwitch; setActive is only a fallback after toggle fails and is itself guarded by PanelBridge.invoke.
